correctness.rationale: Positive support meets both sides. Weight at most three forces one side total to be one and makes every zero on the opposite side invalid. At weight four, side totals are two and two. A zero at \(a_i\) forces \(y_i=0\), and symmetrically, so the supports coincide. A one-index common support violates totality because matched endpoints are nonadjacent; hence exactly two common indices remain and all supported labels are one. The bundled checker exhaustively confirms the complete family through \(n=6\).
